AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #15 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which is recycling? (1 mark)
   A. Burying it
   B. Sending it to sea
   C. Turning used material into something new
   D. Burning it

2. Why should stagnant water be emptied from tins and tyres? (1 mark)
   A. It smells of soap
   B. It is too clean
   C. It cools the compound
   D. Mosquitoes lay eggs in it

3. Which method uses water and a mop? (1 mark)
   A. Dusting
   B. Burning
   C. Mopping
   D. Sweeping

4. Why should you never mix cleaning chemicals? (1 mark)
   A. They become soap
   B. They will look nicer
   C. They can give off harmful fumes
   D. They will cost more

5. What is the correct order for cleaning a room? (1 mark)
   A. Mop, sweep, dust
   B. Mop, dust, sweep
   C. Dust, sweep, mop
   D. Sweep, mop, dust

6. Why should the compound be free of long grass and rubbish? (1 mark)
   A. It looks colourful
   B. To stop rain
   C. To save soap
   D. Snakes, rats and mosquitoes can hide there

7. What is refuse? (1 mark)
   A. Soap
   B. Rubbish or waste
   C. Food
   D. Clean water

8. Which of these is an improvised duster? (1 mark)
   A. A bottle
   B. A tin
   C. A stone
   D. A piece of clean old cloth

9. Which PPE protects the body and clothes from dirt? (1 mark)
   A. Gloves
   B. Dust mask
   C. Overall
   D. Canvas shoes

10. What is the first step in cleaning gumboots? (1 mark)
   A. Knock off lumps of mud outside
   B. Dry them in strong sun
   C. Store them wet
   D. Put them in the fire

11. Why might wet PPE stored away cause a problem? (1 mark)
   A. It becomes lighter
   B. It becomes stronger
   C. It grows mould and smells
   D. It becomes cleaner

12. Why should rubber boots not be dried in very strong heat? (1 mark)
   A. They become cleaner
   B. They grow
   C. The rubber can crack
   D. They get heavier

13. Where should canvas shoes be dried? (1 mark)
   A. In a sealed box
   B. Under wet clothes
   C. In an airy, shady place
   D. In a fire

14. Why should chemicals not be used to clean PPE unless an adult directs you? (1 mark)
   A. They are too cheap
   B. They cool the PPE
   C. They make it too clean
   D. They can harm the skin and the material

15. Which of these is another tacking stitch? (1 mark)
   A. Blanket stitch
   B. Long and short tacking
   C. Herringbone
   D. French knot

16. Which thread colour is best for tacking? (1 mark)
   A. Black on black
   B. One matching the cloth exactly
   C. One that shows clearly on the cloth
   D. White on white

17. What should you do at the end of a sewing lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Count the needles and pins
   B. Throw them
   C. Leave them
   D. Hide them

18. How should you finish a line of tacking? (1 mark)
   A. With a very big knot
   B. With scissors
   C. By pulling the thread out
   D. With a small back stitch

19. How do you place pins for tacking? (1 mark)
   A. Only at the edge
   B. Not at all
   C. Along the line
   D. Across the line

20. Why should tacking thread not be pulled tight? (1 mark)
   A. It will become long
   B. It will not hold
   C. Thread is expensive
   D. The cloth will wrinkle

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. State three safety rules when cleaning PPE. (3 marks)

22. Explain how PPE should be stored and why. (4 marks)

23. Plan a weekly cleaning schedule for the classroom using dusting, sweeping, mopping and refuse disposal. (5 marks)

24. Describe how to make a handkerchief hem using tacking. (4 marks)

25. Name three improvised cleaning tools and what each is made from. (3 marks)

26. Describe how to mop a floor. (4 marks)

27. Describe how to clean canvas shoes. (4 marks)

28. Name three PPE items and say what each protects. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #15 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Turning used material into something new
   Recycling reuses materials.

2. D — Mosquitoes lay eggs in it
   Mosquitoes spread malaria.

3. C — Mopping
   Mopping washes floors.

4. C — They can give off harmful fumes
   Mixing chemicals is dangerous.

5. C — Dust, sweep, mop
   Dust falls, so dust before sweeping.

6. D — Snakes, rats and mosquitoes can hide there
   A tidy compound is safer.

7. B — Rubbish or waste
   Refuse means waste.

8. D — A piece of clean old cloth
   Old cloth makes a duster.

9. C — Overall
   An overall covers the body.

10. A — Knock off lumps of mud outside
   This removes the dirt before washing.

11. C — It grows mould and smells
   Moulds grow in damp places.

12. C — The rubber can crack
   Heat damages rubber.

13. C — In an airy, shady place
   Gentle drying protects the shoes.

14. D — They can harm the skin and the material
   Chemicals can be dangerous.

15. B — Long and short tacking
   Long and short tacking is another type.

16. C — One that shows clearly on the cloth
   It is easy to see and pull out.

17. A — Count the needles and pins
   Counting ensures none is lost.

18. D — With a small back stitch
   Tacking must be easy to remove.

19. D — Across the line
   Pins across the line hold the layers.

20. D — The cloth will wrinkle
   Loose stitches lie flat.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use soap and clean water; keep buckets and brushes from small children; wash your hands after; clean in an open place with drainage.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Clean and dry, in a cupboard, rack or clean box, so it does not grow mould or spread germs, and labelled so it is used by the owner.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for storing, 2 marks for reasons.

23. (5 marks)
   Answer: A table of days with jobs for each learner group: Monday dusting, Tuesday sweeping, Wednesday mopping, and refuse disposal each day, with tools and safety measures.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for jobs, 1 for tools, 1 for safety, 1 for fairness of sharing.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Cut a 25 cm square; fold each edge twice by about 1 cm; pin; tack along the fold with even tacking; check evenness; sew permanently and remove tacking.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Duster from old cloth; mop from strips of cloth on a stick; dustpan from a cut jerrican.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each tool with material.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sweep first; fill a bucket with clean soapy water; squeeze the mop; start from the far corner and mop backwards to the door; rinse the mop; leave the floor to dry with a warning.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: Remove laces; brush off loose dirt; scrub gently with soapy water; rinse; stuff with paper; dry in the shade.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gloves protect hands; gumboots protect feet from mud and water; dust mask protects the nose and mouth from dust.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item with its use.
